```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE)
library(leaflet)
library(dplyr)
```
## Executive Summary

This document presents an interactive geospatial dashboard generated using **R Markdown** and **Leaflet** on `r format(Sys.Date(), '%B %d, %Y')`. 

The interactive map below highlights selected world landmarks, categorized by type, and features:
- Dynamic popups with formatted HTML links and preview information
- Custom OpenStreetMap tile providers
- Clustered marker functionality for dense visual sets

---

## Interactive Map Showcase

```{r leaflet-map}
# 1. Define Landmark Dataset
landmarks <- data.frame(
  name = c("Eiffel Tower", "Statue of Liberty", "Sydney Opera House", "Colosseum", "Taj Mahal"),
  lat = c(48.8584, 40.6892, -33.8568, 41.8902, 27.1751),
  lng = c(2.2945, -74.0445, 151.2153, 12.4922, 78.0421),
  city = c("Paris, France", "New York, USA", "Sydney, Australia", "Rome, Italy", "Agra, India"),
  category = c("Monument", "Statue", "Arts Center", "Amphitheater", "Mausoleum"),
  wiki_url = c(
    "[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eiffel_Tower](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eiffel_Tower)",
    "[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Statue_of_Liberty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Statue_of_Liberty)",
    "[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sydney_Opera_House](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sydney_Opera_House)",
    "[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colosseum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colosseum)",
    "[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taj_Mahal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taj_Mahal)"
  )
)

# 2. Construct Popups with Custom HTML
landmarks <- landmarks %>%
  mutate(
    popup_content = paste0(
      "<div style='font-family: Arial, sans-serif; min-width: 160px;'>",
      "<h4 style='margin-bottom: 4px; color: #2c3e50;'>", name, "</h4>",
      "<b>City:</b> ", city, "<br>",
      "<b>Category:</b> ", category, "<br><br>",
      "<a href='", wiki_url, "' target='_blank' style='color: #3498db; text-decoration: none;'>Read on Wikipedia &rarr;</a>",
      "</div>"
    )
  )

# 3. Build Leaflet Map Pipeline
leaflet(landmarks) %>%
  # Base map tiles (Fully free, no key required)
  addTiles(group = "OpenStreetMap") %>%
  addProviderTiles(providers$Esri.WorldTopoMap, group = "Esri Topo") %>%
  
  # Set default view to focus globally
  setView(lat = 20.0, lng = 10.0, zoom = 2) %>%
  
  # Add interactive markers with popups and clustering
  addMarkers(
    ~lng, ~lat,
    popup = ~popup_content,
    label = ~name,
    clusterOptions = markerClusterOptions(),
    group = "Landmarks"
  ) %>%
  
  # Layer Control for toggling free map styles
  addLayersControl(
    baseGroups = c("OpenStreetMap", "Esri Topo"),
    options = layersControlOptions(collapsed = FALSE)
  ) %>%
  
  # Add visual map enhancements
  addMiniMap(toggleDisplay = TRUE, position = "bottomleft") %>%
  addScaleBar(position = "bottomright")
```

## Data Summary Table

The table below outlines the coordinates and metadata passed directly to the Leaflet widget:

```{r data-table}
knitr::kable(
  landmarks %>% select(Name = name, City = city, Category = category, Latitude = lat, Longitude = lng),
  caption = "Landmarks Location Metadata"
)
```
